rules.legal_concept: Written no-responsive-records notice within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the governmental body determines it has no information responsive to a request, the officer for public information must notify the requestor in writing not later than the 10th business day after the date the request is received.
rules.trigger: Body determines no responsive information exists
rules.clock_spec: 10 business days from receipt of the request
rules.source_language: If the governmental body determines it has no information responsive to a request for information, the officer for public information shall notify the requestor in writing not later than the 10th business day after the date the request is received.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.221(f) (added by HB 4219, 89th Leg., eff. 9/1/2025)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against enrolled HB 4219. Before 9/1/2025 no-records letters were practice, not statute. Post-HB 4219 the 10-bd checkpoint has five exits (produce / certify later date / no-records notice / previous-determination notice / AG-ruling request) - no request may silently close.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice identifying the specific previous determination relied on to withhold
rules.atomic_rule: If the body withholds based on a previous determination, the officer for public information must, not later than the 10th business day after receipt, notify the requestor in writing that the information is being withheld and identify the specific previous determination relied on.
rules.trigger: Body relies on a previous determination to withhold instead of requesting a new AG ruling
rules.clock_spec: 10 business days from receipt of the request
rules.source_language: If a governmental body determines the requested information is subject to a previous determination that permits or requires the governmental body to withhold the requested information, the officer for public information shall, not later than the 10th business day after the date the request is received: (1) notify the requestor in writing that the information is being withheld; and (2) identify in the notice the specific previous determination the governmental body is relying on to withhold the requested information.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.221(g) (added by HB 4219, 89th Leg., eff. 9/1/2025)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against enrolled HB 4219. Pairs with restored TX-0017 (previous-determination exception to the AG-ruling requirement): the exception now carries an affirmative notice duty.

rules.legal_concept: AG-ruling request must state the specific exceptions claimed (wording update to TX-0018)
rules.atomic_rule: The governmental body must ask for the attorney general's decision and state the specific exceptions that apply within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the written request.
rules.trigger: Body wishes to withhold information not covered by a previous determination
rules.clock_spec: 10 business days from receipt of the request (hard; miss = information presumed public under § 552.302)
rules.source_language: The governmental body must ask for the attorney general's decision and state the specific exceptions that apply within a reasonable time but not later than the 10th business day after the date of receiving the written request.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.301(b) (as amended by HB 4219, 89th Leg., eff. 9/1/2025)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26. SUPERSEDES the wording of restored TX-0018 (pre-amendment text said 'the applicable exceptions'; HB 4219 requires 'the specific exceptions'). Kept as its own rule so the frozen wave text stays untouched.

rules.legal_concept: Catastrophe suspension of PIA duties (7 days + one 7-day extension, max 14 calendar days)
rules.atomic_rule: A body currently significantly impacted by a catastrophe may suspend PIA requirements for an initial period of up to 7 consecutive days (once per catastrophe, after submitting notice to the AG on the prescribed form), extendable once by up to 7 more consecutive days; the combined suspension may not exceed 14 consecutive calendar days per catastrophe. Requests received during a suspension are considered received on the first business day after the suspension ends, and pre-suspension requests are tolled until that day.
rules.trigger: Catastrophe significantly impacting the body; catastrophe notice submitted to the AG (remote-work-only situations excluded)
rules.clock_spec: Up to 7 consecutive days + one 7-day extension (max 14 calendar days per catastrophe); requests during suspension deemed received the first business day after it ends; pending-request clocks tolled
rules.source_language: The initial suspension period may not exceed seven consecutive days ... The initial suspension period may be extended one time for not more than seven consecutive days that begin on the day following the day the initial suspension period ends. ... The combined suspension period for a governmental body filing under Subsections (d) and (e) may not exceed a total of 14 consecutive calendar days with respect to any single catastrophe. ... a request for public information received by a governmental body during a suspension period determined by the governmental body is considered to have been received by the governmental body on the first business day after the date the suspension period ends.
rules.source_authority: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.233 (formerly § 552.2325; as amended by SB 1225, 87th Leg., 2021)
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified against enrolled SB 1225 (composite of subsections (d), (e), (g), (i) - ellipses join clauses, each clause verbatim). Desktop research cited the pre-2021 number 552.2325; current codification is 552.233. Clock-matrix design input: a state-gated global pause timer, not a per-request timer.

rules.legal_concept: Request form permitted; clarification for requests lacking reasonable specificity (3-element definition)
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require a requestor to complete a records request form, and may ask the requestor to clarify a request that does not describe the records with reasonable specificity. Reasonable specificity requires: (a) a general time frame of creation/transmission, (b) identifiable records rather than general information, and (c) search terms sufficiently specific to assist the body in identifying the records.
rules.trigger: Request does not describe the requested records with reasonable specificity
rules.source_language: A public body may require a requestor to complete a records request form. If a records request does not describe the requested records with reasonable specificity, a public body may ask the requestor to clarify the request. To have reasonable specificity, a request shall: a. specify a general time frame within which the requested records would have been created or transmitted, b. seek identifiable records, rather than general information without any qualifiers or other specifications, and c. include search terms that are sufficiently specific to assist the public body in identifying the requested records.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against enrolled SB 535 (pp. 8-9). Before SB 535 Oklahoma had no statutory clarification process. Old ¶7 (designated custodians) renumbered to ¶8. No statutory clock attaches (OK has no fixed response deadline).

rules.legal_concept: Specificity denial only after the body has engaged to help identify the records
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be denied for lack of reasonable specificity only if the public body has first engaged with the requestor to seek the information needed to fulfill the request and to identify the records sought - including providing the requestor with general topics or a specific list of records related to the request - and the request is still not reasonably specific.
rules.trigger: Clarification engagement completed and the request remains not reasonably specific
rules.source_language: If a public body has engaged with the requestor to seek the information needed to fulfill the request and to identify the records sought by the requestor, including providing the requestor with general topics or a specific list of records related to the request, the request may be denied if it is still not reasonably specific;
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26; verified verbatim against enrolled SB 535 (p. 9). A codified duty-to-engage/assist gate on the clarification-failure denial path - workflow: clarification round is mandatory before a specificity denial.

rules.legal_concept: Advance payment allowed above $75 estimate or with outstanding fees; excess refunded
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require advance payment of estimated fees when the estimated cost exceeds $75.00 or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests; any portion of an advance payment exceeding the actual cost of responding must be returned to the requestor.
rules.trigger: Estimated cost exceeds $75, or requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests
rules.source_language: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees authorized under this section when the estimated cost exceeds Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00) or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests. Any portion of an advance payment that exceeds the costs of responding to the request shall be returned to the requestor.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26; verified verbatim against enrolled SB 535 (p. 7, underlined new text). Parent-ledger design input: outstanding-fees trigger is cross-request (requestor-level balance), like TX § 552.263(c); refund-of-excess is an accounting obligation.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to respond to a vexatious litigator's request without court leave and a particularized order
rules.atomic_rule: A person subject to a vexatious-litigator order may not request public records without first obtaining leave from the court of common pleas and an accompanying order specifying with particularity what records the person may request; until evidence of both is presented to the public office, the office is under no duty to respond to that person's request.
rules.trigger: Request received from a person subject to a vexatious-litigator order under R.C. 2323.52(D)(1), without evidence of court leave and a particularized order
rules.source_language: A person who is subject to an order entered pursuant to division (D)(1) of this section shall not be permitted to request public records from a public office or person responsible for public records without first receiving both leave to proceed from the court of common pleas as described in this section and an accompanying order from the court that specifies with particularity what public records the person may request from the public office or person responsible for public records. Until the requirements set forth in this division are satisfied and evidence of satisfaction is presented to the public office or person responsible for public records, the public office or person responsible for public records is under no duty to respond to a public records request submitted by a person who is subject to an order entered pursuant to division (D)(1) of this section.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26 via desktop-research recency cross-check; verified verbatim against codes.ohio.gov (April 9, 2025 version). Eligibility-gate family (cf. incarcerated-requester gates and UT vexatious-requester UT-0051..53); the Supreme Court of Ohio maintains the vexatious-litigator list online.

rules.legal_concept: ID may be required when a requester is known or reasonably believed to be a vexatious litigator
rules.atomic_rule: If a public office receives an anonymous records request (or one whose listed name matches) and knows or has reasonable cause to believe the requester is a vexatious litigator, it may require the person to present an acceptable form of identification before responding - an exception to the R.C. 149.43(B)(4) no-identity-condition rule.
rules.trigger: Anonymous or named request where the office knows or reasonably believes the requester is a vexatious litigator
rules.source_language: Pursuant to division (B)(4) of section 149.43 of the Revised Code, if a public office or person responsible for public records receives an anonymous public records request and knows or has reasonable cause to believe that a person who is a vexatious litigator has submitted a public records request, or if, based upon the requestor's listed name, the public office or person responsible for public records knows or has reasonable cause to believe that a person who is a vexatious litigator has submitted a public records request, the public office or person responsible for public records may require that the person present an acceptable form of identification prior to responding to the public records request.
rules.notes: ADDED 2026-07-26; verified verbatim against codes.ohio.gov. Identity/ID config dimension (see requester-class eligibility cluster): Ohio stays no-ID-required EXCEPT this narrow suspected-vexatious carve-out.
